_comment: Packages in an at-scale corpus that pkgxray BLOCKS on a heuristic (non-CVE) finding, where the block is CORRECT/defensible because the package genuinely performs the flagged high-risk operation. These are excluded from the 'heuristic false blocks must be 0' gate the same way known-CVE blocks are — they are true positives a security team SHOULD review, not calibration errors. Keyed by ecosystem so a defensible block in one registry can never silently whitelist a same-named package in another. Each entry must name the exact reason; keep this list minimal and audited. Do NOT add a package here to hide a genuine false positive — fix the detector instead.

npm.pm2: Genuinely installs boot persistence: `lib/API/Startup.js` writes /etc/systemd/system (and upstart/launchd/systemv/openrc) units as its documented `pm2 startup` feature. A process manager that installs system-level boot persistence is exactly what a supply-chain audit should surface for human review; the systemd/init-write BLOCK is the top real-world malware-persistence signal and is deliberately not weakened.

pypi.fastmcp: Genuinely ships a coding-agent auto-exec surface: its sdist includes a root `.claude/settings.json` with an active `hooks` block (SessionStart / PreToolUse) that runs shell commands when a coding agent opens the project — install-time-equivalent code execution. A package that distributes an agent config with live hooks is exactly the agent-supply-chain surface pkgxray exists to surface for human review, so the agent-hook BLOCK is a true positive, not a Python false-fire (the JS-primitive behavioral suite is already gated off Python source). fastmcp arguably should not distribute its developer `.claude` config in the published sdist.
